entries.title: A deferred bead is terminal in fleet-sprint: it blocks its dependents and freezes its parent out of verify
entries.summary: The plan-cap deferral sets status=deferred and nothing in a sprint ever moves it back, while verify eligibility requires every child closed and no unmet blocks edge, so a blocks edge onto a deferred bead dead-ends its dependent and a deferred child permanently blocks its parent from the verify route.

entries.title: test:record with no file argument silently skips every test/slow fixture
entries.summary: node scripts/run-tests.mjs record defaults its node --test target to test/*.test.mjs, so regenerating a bd recording for a test/slow scenario requires naming the file explicitly or the command succeeds while changing nothing.

entries.title: The collision probe fails closed only on the throw path; an exit-0 probe with empty or non-array output still proceeds
entries.summary: The fail-closed classification guards the catch branch only. On the success branch, parseBdJson turns ''/undefined into [] and a non-array JSON body matches no id, so an unexpected exit-0 response is treated as ABSENT and the create goes ahead.

entries.title: bd create --id silently overwrites an occupied id; only a probe-before-create seam prevents it
entries.summary: bd create --id <id> has no built-in collision protection: given an id already held by an open or closed bead it reuses that row and clobbers title/description/priority/type with no error. The safe pattern is to probe (bd show <id> --json) before every explicit-id create and refuse on any positive-or-unknown result.

entries.title: The only real-timer watchdog test lives in test/slow and is not run by npm test, so a withDispatchWatchdog change can regress unnoticed
entries.summary: dispatch-watchdog.test.mjs uses node:test mock timers and cannot catch an unref'd-timer regression; the test that can, test/slow/dispatch-watchdog-timer-ref.test.mjs, is excluded from the default suite by the package.json glob.

entries.title: Dynamic import of a path.join path breaks on Windows; convert with pathToFileURL
entries.summary: import(`${absPath}?t=...`) works on POSIX but on Windows a C:\ path parses as a URL with scheme c: and throws ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME; scripts/check-ascii-only.mjs loadBaseline uses this pattern.

entries.title: A dispatch-pin falsification edit must reuse an existing anchor, or siteFor fails first and masks the real check
entries.summary: siteFor() asserts exactly one matching agent() site before any pin-level comparison runs, so falsifying a pin-collision assertion with an invented anchor string turns the subtest red for the wrong reason and looks confirmed.

entries.title: install --force must stop the registered service, not pkill: launchd/systemd relaunch under a new pid
entries.summary: killApraFleet() signals apra-fleet by process name, which cannot stop a supervised server; the fix is ServiceManager.stop() (graceful exit 0) first, with pid-delta detection to tell a relaunch from a process refusing to die.

entries.title: Live SSE state frame carries the namespace summary and history HTML backfills missing summaries
entries.summary: The viewer SSE 'state' frame payload is {namespace, data, summary}, and the client dispatches workflow:summary:NS before workflow:state:NS. History-mode HTML_TEMPLATE runs backfillExtensionSummaries on the frozen state before embedding it.

entries.title: The shared dispatch-role harness stubs out the watchdog, so timeout tests must re-wire the real one
entries.summary: createRecordingCtx's withDispatchWatchdog only records timeoutS/member/label and returns the dispatch promise unchanged, so any test asserting real watchdog timing through dispatchRole must overwrite ctx.withDispatchWatchdog with the implementation from dispatch-failure.mjs.

entries.title: The Claude agent-install path is not a passthrough and must strip conditional markers
entries.summary: install.ts routes every agent asset through a transform, including Claude; transformAgentForClaude resolves conditional markers with all tools available so markers never ship verbatim.

entries.title: Editing an agents/schemas/*.json contract forces two generated-artifact updates
entries.summary: A role-contract schema change is never a single-file edit: the schema is inlined into auto-sprint.js by a build-time generator with a drift guard, and it is embedded verbatim in the happy-path golden transcript's dispatch prompt.

entries.title: Replacing a content[0] text reader with resultText also closes a false-success in provisionOutcome
entries.summary: provisionOutcome's non-structured fallback tests the extracted text for a leading [FAIL]; an unfiltered content[0] read returns the display banner instead, so a failed provision classified as success.

entries.title: Testing the adaptive stall-probe cadence gate requires advancing fake time between consecutive _poll() calls
entries.summary: Any test that drives StallDetector._poll() more than once and expects each call to actually probe (not be skipped by the per-entry cadence gate) must advance the clock past probeIntervalMs between calls, or the second call is silently skipped.

entries.title: Generic-boundary guard scans fleet-sprint runtime strings, so error messages must not cite apra-fleet source paths
entries.summary: A thrown Error in fleet-sprint that names a path like src/tools/*.ts fails the generic-boundary guard (apra-fleet-repo-internals rule); the same path in a code comment is fine.

entries.title: dispatchRole has 12 call sites for 13 role-policy-table entries by design
entries.summary: doer-resume shares role-policies.mjs's policy object with doer via ROLE_POLICIES['doer-resume'] === ROLE_POLICIES.doer.secondary, and is dispatched from doer's own call site rather than a distinct one, so an inventory of dispatchRole call sites will correctly find 12, not 13, against 13 named roles.

entries.title: The checked-in .beads/issues.jsonl export is stale and must not be used to answer bead-state questions
entries.summary: issues.jsonl in this repo is a passive export last committed 2026-08-18 and contains none of the current sprint's beads, so grepping it for bead state yields silently wrong answers.

entries.title: classifyVerifySet can make a childless verification leaf structurally unreachable by IntegTest
entries.summary: A childless bead created solely to carry an end-to-end/deployed-product verification step can never route to IntegTest, and its parent cannot become verify-eligible while that leaf stays open -- two individually correct eligibility rules combine into a deadlock.

entries.title: Provider abstraction: six adapters, never assume Claude
entries.summary: src/providers/index.ts registers exactly six LlmProvider adapters -- claude, codex, copilot, agy, opencode, none -- matching the LlmProvider union at src/types.ts:4. There is no gemini adapter. Any auth, credential or dispatch change must route through the ProviderAdapter interface rather than assuming Claude-specific fields, and getProvider() defaults to claude only when the argument is null/undefined.

entries.title: OK_REASONS classifies skipped_local_member as ok:true, so callers must check reason before the generic ok/fail branch
entries.summary: src/tools/provision-auth.ts's OK_REASONS array includes 'skipped_local_member' alongside 'ok'/'deployed_unverified'/'deployed_with_errors', so structuredContent.ok is TRUE for a local-member skip. Any consumer branching on structuredContent.ok alone will misclassify a skip as a genuine successful provision.

entries.title: Same-slug callers now open two SqliteProvider handles on one kb.sqlite
entries.summary: Keying the KB provider cache by (slug, repoPath) means two local clones of the same remote get two separate SqliteProvider instances pointed at the same kb.sqlite file; this is safe by design because init sets WAL plus busy_timeout=5000.

entries.title: Armed watchdog budgets must be resolved in both policy() and secondary(), and must name a budget runner.js supplies
entries.summary: role-policies.mjs resolves the watchdog timeoutS sentinel in both policy() and secondary() because the secondary() spread replaces an already-resolved watchdog, and dispatch-role.mjs throws at dispatch time on any budget name ctx.budgets does not supply.

entries.title: bd recordings are keyed by the setup() scenario tag, not by the test filename
entries.summary: scenarioKeyFromCwd derives the recording key from the tempDir basename minus -<millis>-<pid>, which is the setup()/setupMinimal() tag argument, so renaming or moving a mock-sprint test file invalidates no recording; only changing the tag does.

entries.title: A missing-anchor freshness regression surfaces first as kb_list dropping entries, not as a stale-flag assertion
entries.summary: In tests/knowledge/kb-remote-member-e2e.test.ts the four remote-member assertions live in one it(), so removing SqliteProvider's anchorIsMissing guard fails at the SAME DATABASE read-back (line 165) and never reaches the raw stale-row check (line 181).

entries.title: Deriving a crash/corruption journal scenario by mutating a clean recording, instead of re-running a real crashing dispatch
entries.summary: A test needing a 'crashed mid-dispatch' or 'unfinished activity' journal shape can copy a single clean successful recording and post-hoc mutate/truncate the copy, rather than paying for its own separate crashing/hand-written recording leg -- verified equivalent via loadJournal()'s completedByKey/ambiguous outputs.

entries.title: runSprintCycle's sync-bracket extraction needs TWO construction points, not one
entries.summary: openSyncBracketCount is declared at the top of runSprintCycle before command/doltPushMutex/agent exist, so createSyncBrackets must be called there and createGitSync only later, where withGitSync used to be defined.

entries.title: run-integ-suites.mjs runs two serial lanes, not one
entries.summary: The main real-bd lane runs at concurrency 8; a second 'isolated' lane runs after it at concurrency 1, which explains why --status can show pending greater than inflight for a long stretch near the end of a run.

entries.title: bd-replay drift is one-directional, so a regenerated fixture may legitimately shrink
entries.summary: Replay only errors when an issued command has no remaining recorded response; recorded entries that are never consumed are silently ignored, so a refreshed recording with fewer entries than the one it replaces is not evidence of lost coverage.

entries.title: KB provider cache is now keyed by (slug, repoPath), not slug alone
entries.summary: getKbProviders/_providers Map keys on providerKey(slug, repoPath) via a NUL join, so two callers resolving to the same project slug but different repoPath values get distinct provider instances, each anchored at its own caller's repoPath.

entries.title: A guard module added to GUARDED_MODULES must never write 'agent(' or 'command(' inside a backtick template literal on a non-comment line
entries.summary: dispatch-safety-guard.mjs's findCallSites() same-line-string filter (isInsideSameLineString) tracks only single/double quotes, deliberately not backticks, so a template-literal string containing the literal substring 'agent(' or 'command(' on a non-comment line is misdetected as a real call site once that file is itself registered in GUARDED_MODULES.

entries.title: A nested template inside ${...} desyncs maskComments itself, so downstream guards cannot recover
entries.summary: skipStringLiteral() has no notion of template interpolation, so an inner backtick literal inside ${...} ends the OUTER template early and every later literal boundary is off. This corrupts maskComments() output itself, unlike the regex-literal desync.

entries.title: The slow lane runs in bd REPLAY mode despite bypassing run-tests.mjs
entries.summary: npm run test:slow invokes node --test directly, not scripts/run-tests.mjs, but bdMode() defaults to 'replay' when APRA_FLEET_BD_MOCK is unset, so the slow lane still exercises the committed bd recordings and still fails loudly on recording drift.

entries.title: How to falsify a guarded-modules guard test in both directions
entries.summary: Neutering the guard's regex only proves the fixture assertions bite; to prove the CI regression guard is live you must add a real violating call site to a module in the shared GUARDED_MODULES list.

entries.title: The 3-bead golden guard's false-stall signature is [3,3,3]/high-water-4, not the single-bead [1,1,1]/high-water-2
entries.summary: Mutating away the verify-closure close loop in build3BeadFleetApi() does fire a real StalledSprintError, but with a different arithmetic shape than the single-bead file, so pattern-matching on [1,1,1] will miss the 3-bead regression.

entries.title: Four resolveRepoPath helpers exist in src/tools, but only prime and stats ever had the null-to-cwd shape
entries.summary: kb-session-prime.ts and kb-stats.ts returned string|null and degraded to process.cwd(); kb-export.ts and kb-import.ts have always returned string and thrown, so they were never part of the b4g.7 anchor defect despite the bead naming kb-export as a third instance.

entries.title: bd prints literal JSON null, not [], for an empty dolt remote list
entries.summary: `bd dolt remote list --json` emits the JSON literal null when no Dolt remotes are configured. parseDoltRemoteList maps that to [] before its non-array guard, so an unwired repo reads as "no remotes" rather than a parse error; every other non-array shape still throws. Without the null branch, checkDoltRemoteAbsent returns ok:false ("could not parse") for a repo that is simply not wired to a Dolt remote.

entries.title: A nested `node --test` child inside the apra-fleet-se suite must cap its own --test-concurrency
entries.summary: package.json runs the suite at --test-concurrency=8, so any test file that spawns a nested node --test child at the same concurrency doubles peak parallelism and makes wall-clock-budget tests in unrelated files fail intermittently.

entries.title: A behaviour change invalidates a bd replay fixture even when the test text is untouched
entries.summary: bd recordings pin the exact bd command sequence a scenario issues, so changing runner.js behaviour (not the test) makes an already-recorded fixture replay the OLD world and fail confusingly; re-record with the same single-file record command.

entries.title: Local members use host OAuth; provision_llm_auth skips them
entries.summary: Local fleet members share the orchestrator's own machine, so they use whatever OAuth session is already active on that host. provision_llm_auth explicitly skips local members rather than attempting to provision credentials for them.

entries.title: An armed watchdog's timeoutS resolves through maxTotalS, never the inactivity budget
entries.summary: role-policies.mjs's resolveWatchdogTimeout sets an armed watchdog's timeoutS to timeouts.maxTotalS ?? timeouts.timeoutS, so introducing DISPATCH_INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT_S as the first budgets() argument does not reach any watchdog pin.

entries.title: Real dolt failure text reaches the classifier only through bd, and the raw dolt CLI wording is different
entries.summary: classifyDoltFailure parses `bd dolt` output, which re-surfaces dolt errors as 'Error 1105: ...' from dolt_pull()/dolt_push(). The raw dolt CLI emits different text for the same conditions, so fixtures recorded from the CLI do not match the provider rule tables.

entries.title: The wiring test must strip APRA_FLEET_TEST_CONCURRENCY from the child env or it self-masks
entries.summary: Because the wiring test runs inside npm test, the var is already in its own env; without an explicit delete the nested child inherits it and a regressed test script passes green.

entries.title: mock-sprint scenarios run with zero-wait retry backoff, so ladder wall clock is watchdog budgets only
entries.summary: runDevelopLoopScenario sets APRA_FLEET_MOCK_INSTANT_RETRY_BACKOFF=1 for the scenario and restores it in its finally, so any retry-ladder timing derivation must drop the backoff term and must sample the flag from inside the run.

entries.title: A throw from a mocked execute_command is degraded, not propagated, under failSoft
entries.summary: WorkflowEngine._commandDispatch converts a transport-level rejection into { ok: false, error: <message> } when opts.failSoft is set, so a fail-closed throw inside the mock-sprint harness surfaces as a soft failure message rather than unwinding the sprint.

entries.title: What the timing-hazard guard actually catches, and the three ways a sleep escapes it
entries.summary: timing-hazard-guard.test.mjs only flags an unassigned setTimeout with a LITERAL delay of at least 500ms, in three hardcoded files, so a helper-wrapped or parameterized sleep, or a fourth file, is invisible to it.

entries.title: A vitest mock returning the wrong SHAPE hides inside a best-effort try/catch and still reports green
entries.summary: tests/cloud-lifecycle-unit.test.ts stubbed provisionAuth with a bare string while lifecycle.ts read result.structuredContent.ok; the TypeError was swallowed by reProvisionAuth's best-effort catch, so 9 tests passed while every real call failed. Assert on the absence of the warning log, not just on resolves.toBeDefined().

entries.title: The KB scope selector is kbScope(remoteUrl), not scopeOf(repoPath) as bead texts claim
entries.summary: Planning documents describe a repoPath-keyed scopeOf helper, but the real helper keys on the git remote URL and emits repo_remote_url alongside a separately passed repo_path.

entries.title: memory-contract/v1/schemas accepts only generator output; hand-authored schemas live elsewhere
entries.summary: generate-contract.mjs --check fails on any extra or untracked file under schemas/ or bindings/, so a hand-authored schema (e.g. the bible file format) must live outside those dirs, as memory-contract/v1/bible/ does.

entries.title: abort.mjs still classifies pre-sprint refusals by message prefix, which is why their wording is load-bearing
entries.summary: isTypedAbortError's last branch matches err.message.startsWith('Pre-sprint validation failed:'), so the four refusal messages in runSprintCycle are a behavioural contract even now that they are raised as a typed PreSprintValidationError.

entries.title: check-generic-boundary.mjs does not scan fleet-sprint/skills/*.md
entries.summary: ENGINE_FILE_SET covers only js/mjs/cjs under fleet-sprint and md under apra-pm/agents, so SKILL.md files shipped with the engine are never checked for target-specific content.

entries.title: sprint-logs/ must never carry a blanket directory ignore -- .gitignore says so inline
entries.summary: A directory-level rule such as '/sprint-logs/' shadows everything beneath it, un-ignore patterns included, and silently breaks the sprint cost ledger because auto-sprint.js stages it with an unguarded `git add sprint-logs/`. Merged main keeps only scoped rules and records the prohibition as a comment in .gitignore itself, so the lesson survives without depending on the KB.

entries.title: Run a single test file through the bounded runners
entries.summary: Narrow the root runner with APRA_TEST_SUITES_JSON, or pass a file after the mode to apra-fleet-se run-tests.mjs, to keep the wall-clock bound and tree kill without running the whole suite.

entries.title: A deferred stall probe must skip the threshold comparison in the same branch
entries.summary: StallDetector._poll gates the live probe per entry on probeIntervalMs and the skip branch continues before both the probe and the stall-threshold comparison, so a skipped tick is evidence in neither direction.

entries.title: Streak id survives on the beads even though the lane grouping drops it from its return contract
entries.summary: groupStreaksFromLaneMetadata discards the lane id from its return value, but every bead in the returned arrays still carries metadata.streak, so streak identity is recoverable per-bead on that one path.

entries.title: All four kb_ sites now log symmetric rejected and failed lines via isToolError
entries.summary: Supersedes the earlier claim that kb_query was silently swallowing isError results; the only remaining silent case is an unparseable non-error payload.

entries.title: kill(2) only queues the signal: a liveness probe right after killing still sees a live pid on Linux
entries.summary: win-orphan-pipe.mjs killPidTree ends with a bounded synchronous poll (waitForPidGone, waitForGroupGone) because a SIGKILLed process can still be in state S/R at the moment of the probe; the group scan uses ps -e -o pid=,pgid=,stat= filtered in JS.

entries.title: The mock vcs_credential_exec reports a failed dispatch as ok, unlike the real tool
entries.summary: The harness simulator does not wrap its delegate executeCommand call, so the two failure shapes that mock fleet api can produce -- an isError spawn failure and a thrown unmocked-network guard -- do not map to the real tool's dispatch_failed reason.

entries.title: A regionBetween() anchor pair silently widens when the END anchor moves into a later module of the concatenated scan set
entries.summary: execution-role-dispatch-pins builds SRC by concatenating DISPATCH_LADDER_MODULES in order, so moving an end anchor into a phases/* module stretches a one-line region across every module in between -- and the test stays GREEN while measuring almost nothing.

entries.title: shell-command-guard misses shell expansions inside multi-line template literals
entries.summary: segmentLine() in fleet-sprint/shell-command-guard.mjs classifies quoting context one line at a time, so any $VAR, ~/ or $( ) sitting on a continuation line of a multi-line template literal is treated as plain code and never reported.

entries.title: The supervisor's dolt-orphan-sweep arms on a 5-minute interval with no immediate first pass
entries.summary: createDoltOrphanSweep().start() only arms a setInterval(DEFAULT_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS = 5 min) and never runs sweepOnce() eagerly, so a supervisor process that lives under 5 minutes never sweeps at all -- the basis for any time-bounded mitigation of its machine-wide kill scope.

entries.title: ctx.policies is the seam that makes 'this variance is a policy field, not an engine branch' falsifiable
entries.summary: dispatchRole reads its row through ctx.policies when supplied, so a test can splice ONE field of ONE row and observe the engine behave differently; without it the claim that a variance is data rather than a branch cannot be tested at all.

entries.title: The planner retry ladder's pessimistic backoff sum is 50s, not the full 110s ladder
entries.summary: Five attempts have only four inter-attempt gaps, so the planner's 5th configured delay (60000ms) is never reached and the worst-case backoff term is 50000ms.

entries.title: execute_command's input schema is not zod .strict(), unlike execute_prompt's, so a removed field silently strips instead of rejecting
entries.summary: src/tools/execute-prompt.ts's executePromptSchema ends with .strict(), rejecting unrecognized keys, but src/tools/execute-command.ts's executeCommandSchema does not, so removing a field from it does not make zod throw -- the field is just silently dropped from the parsed/validated payload.

entries.title: Routing the PR-raise through vcs_credential_exec drops it out of the workflow journal and activity log
entries.summary: raiseVcsPrForMember's create-PR dispatch moved from the workflow engine's command() path to a raw callTool, so it no longer emits activity events, is no longer journaled/replayable, and loses its dispatch label.

entries.title: sandbox-lock.mjs has no read-only ownership query, so ordering around release is load-bearing
entries.summary: authorizeAndReleaseLock both authorizes and unlinks in one call, and the CLI exposes only acquire/mark-server-started/release -- so any Teardown step placed BEFORE the release runs unconditionally, including against a sandbox owned by a different live run.

entries.title: The decoupled exec timer's never-binds fallback must stay a finite int32 value
entries.summary: EXEC_TIMER_NEVER_BINDS_MS (86_400_000) must not be simplified to Infinity/MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (setTimeout overflow fires immediately) nor to timeout_s (re-couples exec timer to the stall detector).

entries.title: retryBudget() computes remaining max_total_s BEFORE the SERVER_RETRY_DELAY_MS pause, not after
entries.summary: A retry-budget test must burn measurable clock during the FAILING exec call itself, not merely across the fixed 5s retry delay, or 'remaining budget' reads identically to 'full original budget'.

entries.title: Driving all 22 dispatches generically requires resolving a dispatch's owner by object identity, secondary-first
entries.summary: doer-resume is both a table key and the identical frozen object at ROLE_POLICIES.doer.secondary, so a main-first identity lookup tries to drive it by name and fails; scanning for a secondary owner first is what makes a whole-table census possible without a hand-written role map.

entries.title: A sprint-state hoist test must assert constructions AND resolutions, because creating the state alone keeps the construction count at 1
entries.summary: Counting only 'at most one fleet client construction per sprint' passes vacuously when resolveSettleShell is reverted to per-call construction, because createSprintState still builds and logs its own client; the resolution-count half is what actually catches a bypass.

entries.title: A src/tools/ function is not automatically MCP-server-only: src/index.ts routes subcommands straight into them
entries.summary: The register-member CLI subcommand calls the shared registerMember() tool function in a short-lived process, so lifetime/handle arguments that assume every execCommand caller is the long-lived MCP server are wrong.

entries.title: All fleet-sprint ladders are migrated, so both dispatch-pin tables' inline halves are empty and no anchor search runs
entries.summary: PLANNING_LADDERS/EXECUTION_LADDERS contain zero mode:'inline' entries, so planning-role-dispatch-pins.test.mjs pins nothing textually and renaming a ladderAnchor at a real dispatch site does not fail it. The role-policies.mjs ladderAnchor-shadowing hazard is latent, not live.

entries.title: Recording one mock-sprint test file rewrites every scenario fixture in that file
entries.summary: 'node scripts/run-tests.mjs record <file>' re-records the bd fixtures for every scenario the file runs, not just a new one, and record mode can leave the scenario temp dir behind in os.tmpdir.

entries.title: dispatchRole resolves a dispatch's options INSIDE the git-sync bracket, and opts.prepare is why
entries.summary: The engine builds agent() options inside invoke(), i.e. inside withGitSync, because an in-bracket pre-dispatch step can change what the dispatch should say -- the doer's claim narrows its streak after the bracket's D-pull, and the prompt, label and per-bead tier all follow.

entries.title: kb-setup is the one kb tool that takes repo_path but resolves no KB
entries.summary: Fifteen of the sixteen src/tools/kb-*.ts tools spread kbScopeFields and forward repo_remote_url to getKbProviders; kb-setup is excluded by design because its repo_path only locates a .git dir for hook installation and it writes a single global config, never selecting a project KB.

entries.title: Project kb_export throws on an unparseable existing bible instead of overwriting it
entries.summary: readExistingBibleEntries in kb-export.ts throws when .fleet/kb-canonical.json is invalid JSON or has no entries array. The fleet-sprint engine's exportBible treats that as non-fatal, so a corrupt bible silently stops all project-scope exports until it is fixed by hand.

entries.title: Supervisor shutdown stops seams only -- sprint children survive as orphans
entries.summary: POST /api/shutdown and signals run stop(), which closes the HTTP server and stops seams but never kills spawned sprint children; stop a sprint via POST /api/sprints/:id/stop before deleting its directories.

entries.title: Bounded test runners reap nested detached process groups by SIGTERM cooperation, not SIGKILL
entries.summary: On POSIX both run-all-tests.mjs and apra-fleet-se run-tests.mjs spawn detached children, so the inner node --test group is unreachable from the outer runner; the outer runner SIGTERMs its group, waits a grace window, and the inner runner traps SIGTERM to reap its own group.

entries.title: The engine-derived retry.attempts check in role-policies-table is self-referential
entries.summary: role-policies-table.test.mjs feeds the engine retry.attempts+1 failures and then asserts the engine made retry.attempts dispatches, so mutating the shipped value cannot fail that file; the execution pin file is what guards the value.

entries.title: An inline-ladder-guard fixture with no agent() call site is structurally unfalsifiable
entries.summary: findInlineLadderViolations() returns [] at its agentSites.length === 0 early return before the per-role loop, so a test asserting [] on a fixture with no agent() call site passes regardless of mutations to the member-resolution hazard logic.

entries.title: The mock-sprint harness epic stays open at P2, making not-vacuously-strict assertions vacuous
entries.summary: Any mock-sprint assertion of the form 'some final bead is open with priority <= goal' is satisfied by the harness's own scenario epic, which is never closed, so it proves nothing about the bead under test.

entries.title: The mock-sprint harness's default member_detail carries no os field, so every mock sprint exercises the uncached OS degrade
entries.summary: defaultMockCallTool answers member_detail with only vcsProvider, so resolveMemberTarget always throws internally, degrades to { os: 'linux', shell: '' } and never caches -- meaning member_detail is re-dispatched on every settle-shell resolution in mock sprints.

entries.title: Playbook Permissions sections are contract-tested against fleet profiles
entries.summary: tests/integ-playbook-permission-profiles.test.ts asserts every Bash(...) bullet in the playbooks' ## Permissions sections is covered by the composed fleet profiles.

entries.title: The APRA_FLEET_TEST_CONCURRENCY regression site is package.json, not run-tests.mjs
entries.summary: scripts/run-tests.mjs has always exported the concurrency var; the inert-scaledTimeout bug was package.json's test script bypassing run-tests.mjs, so a guard that spawns run-tests.mjs directly cannot catch it.

entries.title: beads-scope wrapCommand only invalidates on a command that RETURNS, not one that throws
entries.summary: The written invalidation contract says every beads-mutating command through the wrapper drops the snapshot, but the wrapper awaits rawCommand first with no try/finally, so a throwing mutation leaves a stale snapshot.

entries.title: apra-fleet-workflow tests now hard-depend on the root dist build
entries.summary: packages/apra-fleet-workflow/test/schema-validated-fake-api.mjs imports the real zod schemas from dist/tools/*.js at module load, so that package's tests cannot run without a prior root npm run build.

entries.title: hasOppositePolarity matches on word-boundary regexes, not substrings
entries.summary: audn.ts hasOppositePolarity tests NEGATIVE_PATTERNS/POSITIVE_PATTERNS with precompiled word-boundary regexes, so "prefixed" no longer collides with "fixed".

entries.title: The harness vcs_credential_exec simulator records into commandLog but never into the workflow activityLog
entries.summary: A command dispatched through defaultMockCallTool's vcs_credential_exec branch reaches mockFleetApi.executeCommand directly, so it appears in commandLog/commandLogDetailed but emits no activity:start event and is invisible to activityLog-based assertions.

entries.title: A single unpaired apostrophe in an objectLiteralFor comment is enough to swallow the real closing brace via later string quotes
entries.summary: Reverting objectLiteralFor's comment-skip branches turns one stray apostrophe in a `//` or `/* */` comment into a phantom string-open; skipStringLiteral then chains through every subsequent quote character in the file (each closing quote is misread as a new opening quote), consuming the literal's real closing brace along the way and returning null instead of a truncated string.

entries.title: resolveFleetServerConnection is a pure descriptor and safe to poll
entries.summary: Despite naming a stdio self-spawn fallback, resolveFleetServerConnection never spawns or connects, so calling it repeatedly in a retry loop is cheap and side-effect free.

entries.title: raiseVcsPrForMember degrades every auth failure, including pre-PR provisioning, instead of throwing
entries.summary: raiseVcsPrForMember (vcs-auth.mjs) catches a provisionPrCapableAuthForMember failure and returns authFailure:true rather than throwing, so both callers (Publish PR in phases/publish-pr.mjs and finalizeAbort in abort.mjs) skip the PR and let the sprint keep its computed verdict; the provider authRemedy hint (azure-devops.mjs AUTH_REMEDY_HINT) is appended to the logged message.

entries.title: An async http.createServer handler that throws kills the apra-fleet server
entries.summary: src/services/http-transport.ts registers an async request handler with no outer try/catch and the server installs no unhandledRejection handler, so any throw in a route terminates the whole process.

entries.title: Windows dispatch completion is process exit plus a drain window, not pipe EOF
entries.summary: On Windows members, local and SSH exec settle on process exit plus a FLEET_EXIT_DRAIN_MS (default 2000ms) drain window, because grandchildren inheriting stdio withhold pipe EOF indefinitely.

entries.title: APRA_FLEET_TEST_CONCURRENCY IS exported by the command CI runs, so scaledTimeout is not inert there
entries.summary: The apra-fleet-se package test script is scripts/run-tests.mjs, which exports APRA_FLEET_TEST_CONCURRENCY=8, so scaledTimeout-derived budgets do scale under npm test; the comment in phase1-leaf-facade-completeness.test.mjs claiming otherwise is stale.

entries.title: Changing ProviderStats silently drifts the kb_stats memory contract
entries.summary: ProviderStats flows unfiltered into the kb_stats MCP response, whose contract schema closes parsed with additionalProperties false, so adding a provider field breaks the published contract while contract:check stays green.

entries.title: runner.js's re-export of fatal-diagnostics.mjs is load-bearing for abort.mjs, not just compatibility sugar
entries.summary: abort.mjs imports findDoltDivergedCause back out of the runner.js facade, so deleting the facade re-export as dead code would break isTypedAbortError and the BEADS_SYNC_CONFLICT terminal state.

entries.title: StallDetector.update() merges, so getEntry alone cannot discriminate per call site
entries.summary: StallDetector.update() does {...existing, ...partial}, so a call site that omits thresholdMs is invisible to a plain getEntry() read; a poison sentinel between transitions is what makes per-site tests discriminate.

entries.title: Exec-level rolling timeout is per-provider via ProviderAdapter.execTimeoutSource()
entries.summary: The timeoutMs handed to strategy.execCommand() in execute-prompt is no longer timeout_s for everyone: claude/agy mirror max_total_s (or a 24h never-binds constant), codex/copilot/opencode/none keep timeout_s.

entries.title: OpenCode's execTimeoutSource() rationale must say dual-signal, not no-pollable-transcript
entries.summary: OpenCode returns 'inactivity_timeout' from execTimeoutSource() like Codex/Copilot, but for a different reason: it is a dual-signal provider (exec timer AND directory-mtime polling), not a no-transcript provider. LLM-facing schema text describing this matrix must not lump it in with the true no-pollable-transcript providers.

entries.title: Viewer SSE /events sends no headers until the first broadcast, so awaiting the http.get response hangs
entries.summary: createDashboardViewer's /events route calls writeHead without writing a body, so Node does not flush headers until the first broadcast. A test that awaits the http.get response callback before emitting an event deadlocks.

entries.title: Execute the generated win32 sweep probe for real by swapping only its Get-CimInstance source
entries.summary: pwsh is cross-platform, so the real generated PowerShell probe can be executed on Linux/macOS by substituting only the Win32_Process source with fabricated objects and shadowing Stop-Process, leaving the entire filter and kill body as real generated text.

entries.title: A configured Dolt sync.remote can be tested with a bare git repo over file://, no dolt or bd binary
entries.summary: beads syncs through refs/dolt/data on a git remote, and dolt-sync.mjs's own tip probe assumes exactly that, so a bare git repo plus a file:// URL is a complete stand-in for a configured sync.remote in unit tests.

entries.title: One anchor policy, three branches: verbatim for read tools, hard-fail for kb_export
entries.summary: kb_session_prime and kb_stats pass a supplied repo_path to getKbProviders verbatim so an unreachable remote anchor stays honestly missing; kb_export deliberately keeps throwing instead, because it writes into repo_path -- and it throws before getKbProviders, so it never anchors at the server cwd either.

entries.title: Vitest module mocks reach through vi.importActual into the actual module's own dependencies
entries.summary: vi.importActual bypasses the mock only for the requested module; its nested imports still resolve through the mocked registry, so a passthrough mock of a dependency can force a branch inside an importActual copy.

entries.title: The inline vcs_token escaper omits the CRT-argv layer that fleet-sprint's PowerShell shQuote applies
entries.summary: escapePowerShellArgInner only doubles single quotes, while fleet-sprint's shQuote also backslash-escapes embedded double quotes for the native CRT parser, so the two halves of a PowerShell create-PR command are escaped by different rules.

entries.title: Regression phase must never abort the sprint, but pre-dispatch provisioning runs outside dispatchRole's catch-all
entries.summary: The regression-test-runner's soft-fail is the role-policies catch-all degrade inside dispatchRole. Anything awaited in runRegressionTestPhase before dispatchRole, such as ensureUnattendedAuto or ensureDeployPermissions, escapes that degrade and becomes a terminal ABORTED that skips Harvest and Publish PR.

entries.title: A sync.remote URL outside SAFE_REMOTE_URL_RE silently disables the dolt remote-tip fingerprint instead of erroring
entries.summary: toGitLsRemoteUrl returns null for any sync.remote with no URL scheme or a character outside [A-Za-z0-9._~:/@+-]; null fails open to a real pull with no fingerprint and no error, so file:// temp-dir test fixtures must gate on that charset.

entries.title: agent-transform.ts and apra-pm install.mjs mirror each other asymmetrically
entries.summary: The .mjs mirror of the conditional-marker machinery differs in naming, division of labour and error class; cross-implementation tests must compare resolveAgentConditionals to the .ts transforms and assert on message text.

entries.title: StallDetector's adaptive probe floor is the loop's own tick interval, not an independent constant
entries.summary: The per-entry adaptive probe cadence in stall-detector.ts's _poll() floors probeIntervalMs at the SAME resolved value start()'s setInterval uses (STALL_POLL_INTERVAL_MS ?? DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL_MS), not at a separate DEFAULT_STALL_PROBE_FLOOR_MS constant, which was deleted along with its STALL_PROBE_FLOOR_MS env var.

entries.title: execute_prompt checks detectUsageLimit after every parseResponse and fails with reason 'usage_limit'
entries.summary: execute-prompt.ts's checkUsageLimit runs provider.detectUsageLimit after all five parseResponse calls (initial dispatch, stale-session retry, overloaded retry, orphan recovery, trust-heal retry), regardless of exit code. On a signal it records the session and returns isError with reason 'usage_limit', a usageLimit block (resumeAt/resumeAtSource/message) and sessionId; it never burns the stale-session or overloaded retries. The workflow layer forwards usageLimit and sessionId onto AgentDispatchError.details unchanged.

entries.title: The regression playbook 18300-series port claim came from a test-only base port, not a product constant
entries.summary: regression-test-playbook.md's old '18300-series fleet-sprint dashboard ports' rationale traces to packages/apra-fleet-se/test/spawner.test.mjs:629, which picks a random base port in 18300-18499 for test isolation. No product constant defines an 183xx range.

entries.title: node:test cancels a test waiting only on an unref'd timer
entries.summary: A test whose only pending work is an unref'd setTimeout (such as beads-view freshForLaunch's timeout) is cancelled with 'Promise resolution is still pending but the event loop has already resolved'; inject a referenced timer through the setTimeout/clearTimeout deps.

entries.title: Node's process.platform is win32 under Git Bash even though the invoking shell is POSIX-like
entries.summary: A Node script invoked from Git Bash on Windows sees process.platform === 'win32' (native node.exe), so platform-detection in a helper script should branch on process.platform, never on which shell/tools (lsof, pgrep) happen to be on PATH -- that lets a script correctly pick the Windows-native probe (netstat/taskkill, Get-CimInstance) even when run from a POSIX-shaped shell.

entries.title: Falsify a phases/* slice by set-diffing against the pre-commit runner.js in both directions
entries.summary: Extract the regions from `git show HEAD:<runner.js>` rather than the diff's minus-lines, normalise whitespace and sort, then run comm both ways: one direction proves nothing was dropped, the other proves nothing but scaffolding was added.

entries.title: A crossing sync-bracket close can never be the last open bracket, so the pause-guard poke is unreachable there
entries.summary: withOpenSyncBracket's CROSSING-close branch is entered only while another bracket sharing the key is still open, so openSyncBracketCount is always >= 1 after the decrement and the count===0 pause-guard poke cannot fire on that path.

entries.title: dist-pm does not prune orphaned dist/agents schemas, so the dist staleness guard can fail in a way dist-pm cannot fix
entries.summary: The dist/agents/schemas staleness guard tells you to run npm run dist-pm, but dist-pm copies without pruning, so a dist-only orphan left by another branch survives the refresh and the guard keeps failing until the file is deleted by hand.

entries.title: A facade re-export test must use namespace imports, or a dropped export fails as a SyntaxError
entries.summary: A test that asserts runner.js still re-exports moved symbols must read them off a namespace import; a static named import turns a dropped re-export into a module-load SyntaxError that kills the file before any assertion runs.

entries.title: kill-port.mjs owns the playbook's bounded-retry port-guard semantics, so playbook guards are one-liners
entries.summary: Every regression-playbook port guard (18700, 18701, 3001) is a single kill-port.mjs invocation; the 5s bounded retry, re-kill-each-pass, probe-tool hard-fail and fail-loud exit all live in waitPortFree(), not in the playbook's shell.

entries.title: vcs-auth.mjs's facade pin fails on ADDED top-level symbols, not just removed ones
entries.summary: vcs-auth-extraction-facade.test.mjs asserts its two MOVED_*_SYMBOLS lists and vcs-auth.mjs's top-level declarations agree symbol-for-symbol, so introducing a new top-level helper turns the gate red exactly like deleting one does.

entries.title: inline-ladder-guard no longer skips an unresolvable member kind silently -- it throws, so the two older KB entries saying otherwise are stale
entries.summary: memberExprFor() resolves pool-head and runtime bindings and findInlineLadderViolations() throws for any dispatch with a member it cannot resolve, so entries describing a silent skip no longer describe the tree.

entries.title: The .trim() guard in resolveProjectSlug is provably redundant and cannot be pinned by any test
entries.summary: project-slug.ts guards its remote-URL short-circuit twice, but the outer remoteUrl.trim() check is unreachable-by-effect given slugify, so no input can distinguish its removal and no regression test can pin it.

entries.title: A verbatim extraction out of runner.js breaks textual test anchors in unrelated test files, and the re-anchor has two halves
entries.summary: Tests that assert against a raw fs.readFileSync of runner.js desync on a move-only extraction even though the code is byte-identical; re-pointing the assertion is only half the fix, the now-dead source read and its comments must go too.

entries.title: kb_export description text lives in five places; the binding is generated
entries.summary: The kb_export tool description is duplicated in tool-registry.ts, generate-contract.mjs, INVENTORY.md (twice) and the generated binding JSON; edit the sources and regenerate.

entries.title: dispatchReview has exactly two consumers, Review and Re-Review, not three
entries.summary: Final Review does not receive dispatchReview -- it only cites it in a boilerplate comment that six other phase modules also carry, so a grep for the identifier across phases/ badly overcounts its real consumers.

entries.title: Installer step labels are derived by arithmetic offsets from totalSteps, so inserting a step misnumbers silently
entries.summary: src/cli/install.ts computes late step labels (workflows, Dolt, Beads, KB) as offsets from totalSteps, with nothing cross-checking them against a counter.

entries.title: list_members host field is a formatted host colon port composite
entries.summary: list_members json emits host via formatAgentHost, so it is a combined host:port string for remote members and a sentinel for local/relay members.

entries.title: Balanced-paren scans of runner.js must mask comments first or call ranges run away to EOF
entries.summary: runner.js prose comments contain apostrophes, which a string-skipping paren scanner reads as an opening quote; it then swallows real code including closing parens, so a call site's balanced range silently extends to end-of-file.

entries.title: shell-command-guard false-positives on nested templates and on any dollar-word in prose strings
entries.summary: The guard flags constructs in ANY JS string, not just member-bound command strings (a dollar-word in prose trips it), and segmentLine() is single-line and mis-tracks nested template literals. Registering a fleet-sprint sibling in GUARDED_MODULES therefore needs per-line "shell-guard-allow: <reason>" comments on the false positives (as contracts.mjs and vcs-module.mjs do); modules that cannot be scanned clean go in GUARD_REGISTRATION_EXEMPT.

entries.title: Moving a phase body into a module loses in-flight reassignments on the throw path, and runSprintCycle is what makes that safe
entries.summary: A phase module that reassigns params and returns them keeps success-path semantics exactly, but drops partial assignments if it throws mid-phase; that is unobservable only because no try/catch sits between the phase call sites and the Cycle Evaluation reads.

entries.title: kill-port netstat parsing depends on the colon-anchored port suffix
entries.summary: parseNetstatPids matches the local address with endsWith(':<port>'); the leading colon is what stops port 3001 from also matching netstat rows for 13001/23001/53001.

entries.title: Falsify a root-repo vitest test with a detached git worktree, not a scratch copy
entries.summary: A tests/*.ts file needs the whole project graph, so the copy-a-directory-to-tmp pattern does not work; add a detached worktree, symlink node_modules into it, revert the impl there, and run npx vitest from inside it.

entries.title: Watchdog never auto-declares a live-PID child crashed, by design
entries.summary: watchdog.mjs classifies a live PID as running-healthy or running-unresponsive by HTTP signal and never as crashed; late-failure visibility must come from the child's recorded terminal state, not by weakening the classifier.

entries.title: The smoke test's supervisor uptime bound is enforced in Test scenario step 4, not in Teardown
entries.summary: Teardown's SUPERVISOR_UPTIME >= 300 check only prints a warning; the actual enforcement of the dolt-orphan-sweep mitigation is step 4's UPTIME_DEADLINE = SUPERVISOR_STARTED_AT + 280 hard-stop, so any regression test must assert on the 280s branch.

entries.title: Machine callers of MCP tool results must skip the onboarding preamble block
entries.summary: wrapTool can prepend an <apra-fleet-display> onboarding block ahead of a non-JSON result, so programmatic consumers must not JSON.parse content[0].text blindly.

entries.title: raiseVcsPrForMember sends exactly one of repo/repoRef, never both
entries.summary: The PR-raise call into buildCreatePrCommand spreads either {repoRef} or {repo} but never both, because a multi-part canonical repo string would override repoRef coordinates and mis-encode the Azure DevOps request URL.

entries.title: Backlog-role alias is rewritten in the CLI, so the runner learns of it only via args.roleMapWarnings
entries.summary: bin/cli.mjs resolveRoleMapWithWarnings folds roleMap.orchestrator into roleMap.backlog before buildRunnerArgs, so the runner's run-log deprecation warning depends on roleMapWarnings being forwarded; the supervisor forwards the alias-intact map to the child CLI.

entries.title: merge-kb-canonical identity is the entry id only; title and source_file_hashes are content
entries.summary: packages/apra-fleet-se/scripts/merge-kb-canonical.mjs matches bible entries across base/ours/theirs by id only (no title fallback); title and source_file_hashes are in CONTENT_FIELDS; id-less entries throw MalformedInputError (CLI exit 2) and duplicate ids are conflicts (exit 1).

entries.title: Manufacture a deterministic POSIX zombie with sh -c '<child> & echo $!; exec sleep N'
entries.summary: To test zombie-aware liveness checks, spawn sh -c with a background child and exec sleep so the new parent never reaps; poll ps -o stat= until it starts with Z.

entries.title: The stall_poll_tick summary line is JSON plus an elapsed suffix, not parseable JSON
entries.summary: LogScope.ok() appends ' elapsed=Nms' after the payload, so the per-tick probe-count summary cannot be JSON.parse()d whole, unlike the per-entry lines in the same scope.

entries.title: To see a node --test worker in the process table, put the marker in the test file name
entries.summary: node --test workers carry only node argv plus the test file path, so an env-var marker is invisible to process-table checks; embed the marker in the fixture file name, and exclude the PowerShell query's own pid.

entries.title: renderDegradeNote throws on a missing template, so degrade.classes and degrade.noteTemplates must move together
entries.summary: Adding an error class to a row without adding its note template turns a survivable degrade into an uncaught throw out of dispatchRole; the only thing preventing it is one test.

entries.title: Windows symlinkSync with type dir fails EPERM without symlink privilege; junction works
entries.summary: On this Windows dev box fs.symlinkSync(target, path, 'dir') throws EPERM while type 'junction' succeeds, so apra-fleet-se falsification tests that symlink node_modules into a temp sandbox fail under npm test.

entries.title: vitest resolves a missing named export to undefined, but node --test hard-fails the whole module
entries.summary: Under Vite's SSR transform a missing named import becomes undefined and the module body still runs, so only tests that call it fail; plain Node ESM raises a link-time SyntaxError and nothing in the file runs.

entries.title: A supervisor readiness probe must check GET /api/health pid identity, not just that the port answers
entries.summary: The supervisor fails (no fallback port) when its port is taken, so a successful curl only proves something is listening; /api/health returns the answering process pid, which is what makes readiness an identity check.

entries.title: apra-fleet-se test:slow bypasses run-tests.mjs and gets none of its runner-level behaviour
entries.summary: test:slow is a raw node --test invocation, so it has no wall-clock bound, no --test-concurrency, and no APRA_FLEET_TEST_CONCURRENCY export; runner hardening in run-tests.mjs does not cover it.

entries.title: Supervisor sprint-row progress is pulled from each child's GET /state?summary=1, never recomputed
entries.summary: dashboard.mjs buildSprintViews() no longer computes progress from the supervisor's own beads clone; it pulls each child's published summary concurrently, classifies it (ok/unreachable/no-summary/unavailable), and caches the last good summary in memory per sprintId.

entries.title: Member OS resolution: always via agent.os
entries.summary: The orchestrator and each fleet member can independently run Windows/Mac/Linux -- local members share the orchestrator's own OS, but remote members can be any OS regardless of the orchestrator's. Never assume a target member's shell/OS matches the orchestrator's.

entries.title: plan-reviewer findings: empty array means plan-wide, absent means pre-contract
entries.summary: The new optional findings field distinguishes an empty array (explicit plan-wide objection) from an absent field (verdict predates the contract), which is what lets the contested-bead consumer migrate off prose scanning without changing behaviour.

entries.title: Setup shell's $$ is unsafe to record for liveness checks under Git Bash on Windows
entries.summary: scripts/sandbox-lock.mjs's acquire CLI previously recorded the Setup shell's self-reported $$, which under Git Bash on Windows is an MSYS-internal pid invisible to defaultDeps.isAlive's native process.kill(pid,0) check -- fixed by having the CLI record its own process.ppid instead, since the CLI process is itself a direct child of the Setup shell and process.ppid always resolves in the native OS pid namespace.

entries.title: bd-replay record mode bypasses the real-mode caches, so recordings are 1:1 with issued calls
entries.summary: runCmd applies the dolt-sync/sync.remote/read caches only when bdMode() === 'real'; record mode sends every bd call other than dolt-sync and the synthesized ones (bd where, bd memories --json, bd forget) to recordBd, and recordBd rewrites the whole fixture with writeFileSync rather than appending.

entries.title: apra-fleet start's already-running reuse path exits before rewriting server.json
entries.summary: src/index.ts exits 0 on a live instance before createHttpTransport and the server.json write, so a no-op start never refreshes server.json; the recorded port is the only way to detect a wrong-port instance.

entries.title: After a handled terminating signal, run-all-tests.mjs deferred hard-kill timer must own the exit
entries.summary: The group SIGTERM reaps the shell:true wrapper quickly, so the suite loop would fall through to the trailing process.exit before the deferred killTree; deferredExitPending gates that exit and the timer kills the pgid captured at signal time.

entries.title: resolveFleetServerConnection falls back to stdio instead of throwing when no HTTP singleton is running
entries.summary: The client resolver throws for an unreachable server only when APRA_FLEET_TRANSPORT=http is set; by default it returns a stdio self-spawn resolution, so "server not started yet" is not an exception path.

entries.title: explicit-id-create guard now uses a call-expression-agnostic command-literal rule, unioned with the command() site rule
entries.summary: The guard no longer depends on findCallSites recognising the enclosing call identifier. A second rule flags any string literal whose content begins with the bd create command and continues into an argument, so wrappers, renamed bindings and method calls are covered.

entries.title: provisionOutcome's prose fallback in vcs-auth.mjs is live and deliberately pinned
entries.summary: An earlier KB entry calling that fallback dead code and constant-true is wrong: the [FAIL] prose regex still fires even though wrapTool never sets isError, and two tests pin the behaviour.

entries.title: ServiceManager.stop is a graceful HTTP shutdown with its own 5s window, then a SIGTERM that re-arms launchd KeepAlive
entries.summary: On macOS and Linux, ServiceManager.stop delegates to gracefulStopByServerJson (POST shutdown, 5s poll, SIGTERM fallback) and never unloads the job; a SIGTERM fallback can trigger a supervisor relaunch.

entries.title: Local vs remote member dispatch paths
entries.summary: Local members share the orchestrator's own machine and credentials, so no SSH or file probe is needed -- check agent.agentType === 'local' and short-circuit. Remote members require actual SSH connectivity and credential probes.

entries.title: Verify a move-only runner.js extraction by normalized line-set diff plus a runtime export-surface diff
entries.summary: Two mechanical checks prove a fleet-sprint move-only extraction without reading the moved code: set-compare the removed lines against the new module after normalizing comment prefixes and the export keyword, then import the old and new runner.js side by side and diff Object.keys.

entries.title: Structured tool response shapes are pinned to the client typedefs by a ROOT vitest test
entries.summary: tests/structured-tool-responses.test.ts check 4 diffs four server *Fields interfaces against api.mjs typedefs both ways, so a new structuredContent field without the client typedef turns root npm test red.

entries.title: Not every bd list --parent read in fleet-sprint needs closed children -- only computeChildFloor does
entries.summary: computeChildFloor must count CLOSED children (id-floor / re-mint prevention) so it passes --all, while phases/plan.mjs pending-rejected-newTask reconciliation and parent-notes-staleness.mjs deliberately read only default (open) children.

entries.title: role-policies.mjs's secondary() dispatch inherits its main dispatch's member field unless explicitly overridden
entries.summary: secondary(main, role, kind, over) spreads ...main first, so a role's resume/re-ask dispatch shares the SAME member object as its main dispatch for every role in the table today -- any consumer matching dispatches by member-routing expression must de-duplicate across [entry, entry.secondary] or it double-counts one real call site.

entries.title: A source-level watchdog explicitness check must resolve secondary-declared roles to their base row
entries.summary: ROLE_NAMES includes doer-resume, which is declared via secondary(doer, 'doer-resume', ...) and has no policy('doer-resume', ...) literal, so a per-role source scan for an explicit watchdog declaration fails unless it follows the secondary back to its base.

entries.title: Three distinct git-credential-helper file shapes exist across member OS/shell combinations
entries.summary: The deployed credential helper differs by member OS AND shell: POSIX (linux/macos) writes an extensionless $HOME script, windows-powershell writes $env:USERPROFILE\...bat, and windows-gitbash writes a .bat under $HOME but is invoked through bash -- so any read-side builder needs all three forms plus the PowerShell call operator.

entries.title: A directly launched sprint's deployer self-id is the branch name, not a ledger uuid
entries.summary: runner.js derives the deployer's own reservation id as validated.runId || validated.branch, so a standalone (non-supervisor) launch hands the deployer a branch name rather than a supervisor sprintId.

entries.title: Falsify a fleet-sprint or root-repo test without ever mutating the tracked tree
entries.summary: Copy the module directory to /tmp and revert the single file there, or reconstruct a pure function in a standalone script -- mutating tracked source in place risks a torn read under the concurrent suites and can leave the file corrupted.

entries.title: bd show on a missing id exits 1, so every fleet-sprint existence probe lands in its catch branch
entries.summary: bd show <missing-id> --json exits 1 with an error envelope rather than returning [], and FleetWorkflow.command() throws on any non-zero exit, so an existence probe's catch branch is the NORMAL path, not the rare one.

entries.title: The mock-sprint and golden suites leak temp files, so 'no artifacts outside the sandbox' cannot be shown by running them
entries.summary: One full mock-sprint pass leaves exactly 10 fleet-sprint-body-*.txt files in the system temp dir and the golden 3-bead suite leaves one sprint-lock entry, independently of any gate that spawns them; npm test already does this twice today.

entries.title: Supervisor shutdownRequested resolves only after full teardown
entries.summary: server.mjs stop() is idempotent and calls shutdownResolve() last, after server.close() and every seam stop, so code after `await supervisor.shutdownRequested` in bin/serve.mjs runs strictly last for both the signal and the /api/shutdown paths.

entries.title: Project-scope kb_export is additive and basis-filtered; global scope still rewrites
entries.summary: kb_export scope=project never removes or rewrites existing bible entries and adds only CONFIRMED entries whose source_file_hashes basis matches the files on disk; with nothing to add it leaves the file untouched. Global scope still rewrites from the live CONFIRMED set.

entries.title: gitRepos is an access list; only a single URL-shaped entry is a usable origin
entries.summary: agent.gitRepos is declared optional string[] and usually holds bare "Owner/Repo" access identifiers, not clone URLs. knownRepoRemoteUrl (in src/services/member-remote-url.ts, re-exported from execute-prompt.ts) returns a URL only when gitRepos has EXACTLY one entry AND it is URL-shaped (contains "://" or starts with "git@"); anything else yields undefined rather than a guessed URL.

entries.title: Streaks are anonymous bead arrays by the time they reach the doer dispatch, so the sync bracket carries no streak identity
entries.summary: groupStreaksFromLaneMetadata discards metadata.streak after grouping, selectStreaks never has a lane id, and the harvester has no streak -- so streak identity is unavailable on 2 of 3 pushCode:true paths, and there is no per-streak branch to key exclusivity on. Doer streak turns are serialized by globalDoerTurn in phases/develop.mjs.

entries.title: A role's member expression in role-policies.mjs is not role-unique, so it cannot identify a ladder
entries.summary: Three distinct roles share roleMember('planner') and two share roleMember('plan-reviewer'), so any guard that identifies a role's inline dispatch by its member routing expression alone flags other roles' ladders too.

entries.title: apra-fleet-client's createWorkflowEngine() is dead code -- workflow/ dir does not exist in that package
entries.summary: packages/apra-fleet-client/src/client/factory.mjs's createWorkflowEngine imports '../workflow/index.mjs' relative to itself, but apra-fleet-client's own src/ tree has no workflow/ directory in this repo state -- any caller must build the client manually (StdioTransport + McpClient + ApraFleet) instead.

entries.title: Slicing a runSprintCycle phase: pass reassigned locals both IN and OUT so the call site needs no conditional
entries.summary: Destructured parameters are assignable in JS, so a moved phase body can keep its `x = ...` statements byte-identical if the caller passes x in and destructures it back out -- which also makes the skip path a no-op without an `if`.

entries.title: The dispatchRole engine must spell agent( and ctx.withGitSync( literally or the guards lose it
entries.summary: dispatch-role.mjs destructures agent from ctx so the guards' call-site regexes still match its one dispatch, while the bracket and watchdog stay ctx-qualified and are asserted by regex instead.

entries.title: serve.mjs self-executes via isMainModule but exports no selfExecuting flag, so the workflow trampoline mis-handles it
entries.summary: serve.mjs runs serveMain() when argv[1] is itself, but exports no selfExecuting/main/run/default; runWorkflow() rewrites argv then reports did-not-execute, and calling serveMain() after rewriting argv starts two supervisors.

entries.title: makeTestLocalAgent defaults member os to the host platform, silently neutering OS-forcing test mocks
entries.summary: tests/test-helpers.ts makeTestLocalAgent sets os from process.platform, so a mock that forces a Windows-only branch is a no-op on a Windows runner and untested there.

entries.title: exec-bd helpers resolve bd through the npm Windows shim; shell:true paths remain on Windows
entries.summary: Two drifted near-duplicate exec-bd helpers resolve bd on Windows via npm's generated bd.cmd shim; when no shim exists, execBdSync falls back to a shell:true invocation with no argument validation, and execBdAsync always uses shell:true behind assertSafeArgs.

entries.title: sandbox-deploy allocatePorts rejects adjacent port pairs, so fixed test fixtures must not use consecutive ports
entries.summary: allocatePorts() now rejects any candidate within abs-diff 1 of an already-chosen port (Math.abs(p - port) <= 1, which also subsumes the old exact-duplicate check), because the observed sandbox collision handed back a consecutive fleet/supervisor pair.

entries.title: An escaped backtick in any GUARDED_MODULES file trips the shell-command guard, even inside an Error message
entries.summary: shell-command-guard.mjs flags an ESCAPED backtick (a literal backtick inside a template literal) on any non-comment line of a guarded fleet-sprint module as backtick command substitution, even when it is prose in a thrown Error; unescaped backticks inside quoted strings are deliberately not flagged.

entries.title: kb-reconcile-e2e fixture's import-source bible is also kb_export's target file
entries.summary: tests/knowledge/kb-reconcile-e2e.test.ts writes its merged branch-B import fixture to <repo>/.fleet/kb-canonical.json, the same path kbExport writes, so any change to kb_export merge semantics treats every fixture entry as already in the bible.

entries.title: Only roles with a kb-apply post-result step have their kb_captures recorded; the KB block no longer promises it to others
entries.summary: A dispatched role kb_captures output is applied only if its role-policies.mjs row lists kb-apply in postResult; planner, plan-reviewer, scoped-replan roles, deployer, integ-test-runner and regression-test-runner have none. The agent() wrapper now passes captureChannel=agentTypeAppliesKbCaptures(agentType) to kbKnowledgeBlock, so those roles are told to note findings in their own report instead of being promised the orchestrator records kb_captures; a persona shared across rows counts as no channel unless every row has kb-apply.

entries.title: openSyncBracketCount is a pure aggregate counter; cross-owner bracket overlap is legitimate except the opt-in code-write key
entries.summary: git-sync.mjs createSyncBrackets counts open brackets with no owner awareness; overlap across members is legitimate by default (D-push is serialized by the dolt push mutex). Only brackets passing exclusiveKey (CODE_WRITE_BRACKET_KEY, used by pushCode:true withGitSync) are tracked on a per-key stack and throw ConcurrentSyncBracketError on a crossing close. What keeps code-writing dispatches from overlapping is the globalDoerTurn FIFO gate in phases/develop.mjs; the exclusive key is a backstop for it being broken.

entries.title: execFileSync distinguishes a timeout from a non-zero exit by error.code, not error.status
entries.summary: A timed-out execFileSync sets code ETIMEDOUT, signal SIGTERM and status null, while a non-zero exit leaves code undefined and sets status to the exit code with stdout and stderr intact.

entries.title: VCS provider builders key the curl binary on os and the quoting dialect on shell
entries.summary: In fleet-sprint VCS provider builders, os selects the curl BINARY (curlBinary, OS-keyed) while shell selects the QUOTING DIALECT (shQuote, shell-keyed with an OS fallback); a windows+gitbash member correctly gets curl.exe with POSIX quoting.

entries.title: Extracting a fleet-sprint module out of runner.js breaks dispatch-safety-guard's EXPECTED_COMMAND_COUNT
entries.summary: test/dispatch-safety-guard.test.mjs hard-asserts the number of command()/agent() call sites in runner.js, so any move-only extraction that carries a command() call site out of runner.js fails that test even though every site stays compliant.

entries.title: Adding any duplicated top-level string to viewer state can turn plain /state fields into $ref markers
entries.summary: buildListStatePayload() dedupes every string of 24+ chars that occurs 2+ times anywhere in the payload, top-level fields included. Copying runId or timestamps into a new top-level object turns state.runId into {$ref:n} for consumers that read /state without resolveStringRefs.

entries.title: guarded-modules-coverage's isAccountedFor() must compare full relative paths, not basenames, to avoid a nested-module collision
entries.summary: Per-guard violation-count baselines correctly compare by basename (guards report violations via path.basename), but the separate 'is every module registered at all' completeness sweep must compare full relative paths, because a nested file (e.g. phases/index.mjs) can share a bare filename with an unrelated top-level registered module (vcs-providers/index.mjs) and would otherwise be silently treated as already covered.

entries.title: Do not dynamically import every runner.js importer -- scripts/dolt-settle-integration.mjs runs main() at module scope
entries.summary: A test that imports each importer of fleet-sprint/runner.js to prove resolution will fire a live MCP connection and real dolt operations from that one file.

entries.title: install --force restarts a service it stopped, once the binary copy finishes
entries.summary: If the --force guard stopped a registered service, install restarts it after the binary copy (or lets the final service step re-register/start it), and always prints the restart command.

entries.title: Lockfile drift is invisible to npm test
entries.summary: A PR review that runs only 'npm test' cannot catch package.json/package-lock.json drift (e.g. a dependency override added to package.json without regenerating the lockfile), because npm test runs against whatever node_modules is already populated. Only 'npm ci' -- the reproducible-install path CI actually uses -- reproduces that failure.

entries.title: A blocks edge inside a streak lane splits the lane instead of sequencing it
entries.summary: groupStreaksFromLaneMetadata groups only the CURRENT ready set, so two co-laned beads joined by a blocks edge are never ready together and the lane degrades to one bead per round. streakOrder, not blocks, sequences work inside a lane.

entries.title: wrapTool already accepts { text, structuredContent }, so adding a structured MCP response needs no tool-registry change
entries.summary: src/services/tool-registry.ts's wrapTool is typed to accept string | { text, structuredContent }, so converting an existing tool from a plain-string return to a structured one requires no edit at the registration site -- only the tool file and its direct consumers.

entries.title: retry.infraResumeAttempts is a boolean gate, not a count -- a value above 1 is silently ignored
entries.summary: The engine reads infraResumeAttempts only as `> 0`; the resume loop bound comes from retry.resumeAttempts, and the loop re-iterates only on a repeated max_turns exhaustion, never on a repeated infra failure.

entries.title: The fleet-sprint goal-scope reopen guard was inert: 'P2' string compared against a numeric bead.priority
entries.summary: runner.js's goalMax is goalPriorityMax()'s STRING form ('P2') but the reopen guard compared it to a numeric bead.priority, so `3 > 'P2'` was a NaN comparison and the guard never skipped anything at any verdict site until normalizeGoalMax() was added.

entries.title: registerAllTools can be driven by a 4-line fake McpServer, unlocking every handler body for testing
entries.summary: The 'no test loads tool-registry.ts' gap is structural but trivially closable: a fake with tool()/server.sendLoggingMessage() records every registered handler and runs in ~2s.

entries.title: Mutate GUARDED_MODULES via a node --import preload to test guard registration without editing files
entries.summary: GUARDED_MODULES is a const binding but a mutable array, so a preload can append to it and exercise the guard tests against a larger registry with the working tree untouched.

entries.title: Node ESM circular imports between runner.js and its extracted fleet-sprint siblings are safe when confined to function bodies
entries.summary: Verified directly (a standalone a.mjs<->b.mjs repro, then live in prompts.mjs/worklists.mjs/abort.mjs) that a module split out of runner.js can import a still-runner.js-resident helper back, and vice versa, without any load-order failure, as long as neither side references the other's binding at top-level module-evaluation time.

entries.title: tests/install-force.test.ts afterEach does not actually restore process.platform
entries.summary: Its afterEach redefines process.platform to its own current value, so a platform set by one test leaks into every following test in the file.

entries.title: The ASCII-only gate fails on shrink, so baselining generated files is a trap
entries.summary: check-ascii-only.mjs evaluate() fails on new-file, ratchet AND shrink findings; a baselined file that loses non-ASCII characters (or is deleted) turns npm test red until ascii-baseline.mjs is edited, and .beads/issues.jsonl is baselined even though bd regenerates it.

entries.title: The default VCS credential label's derivation is unfalsifiable by value, only by source shape
entries.summary: Re-hardcoding vcs-auth.mjs's DEFAULT_VCS_CREDENTIAL_LABEL to the literal 'github' left the whole test suite green, because DEFAULT_VCS_PROVIDER is itself 'github'; only a source-level assertion on the assignment (phase2-flagged-behaviour-gating.test.mjs) can gate it.

entries.title: degrade.classes, not degrade.kind, decides what a ladder fabricates -- and the integ runner's omission of 'infra' is the whole INCONCLUSIVE variance
entries.summary: The engine fabricates a value only for the ERROR_CLASSES a row lists in degrade.classes. The integ row lists schema and dispatch but deliberately NOT infra, which is what turns an envelope-less failure into an `inconclusive` record instead of a false passed:false.

entries.title: ClaudeProvider.detectUsageLimit treats a bare 429 as a usage limit without the limit-message
entries.summary: A 429 apiErrorStatus is classified as a usage limit on its own; the 'hit your <...> limit' message is only required for the non-429 terminalReason==='api_error' path.

entries.title: test/helpers/dispatch-pin-scanner.mjs has its own maskComments that does not model regex literals
entries.summary: The regex-literal desync fixed in fleet-sprint/dispatch-safety-guard.mjs still exists in the pin scanner's own maskComments, which drives the dispatch-pin and role-policy census tests; it is latent until a quote-bearing regex lands in a DISPATCH_LADDER_MODULES file.

entries.title: The client package carries a second hand-maintained copy of every tool field description
entries.summary: packages/apra-fleet-client/docs/api-reference.md has its own hand-written per-field glosses for tool parameters; nothing generates or tests it, so it drifts silently.

entries.title: pushBeadsAfter's real gap vs doltPushAfter was the non-throwing degrade contract, not retry/lease-renewal (those already lived inside doltPushAfter itself)
entries.summary: doltPushAfter() already contains retry (via runDoltStep's maxTransientRetries), mutex lease renewal, and settle-callback support regardless of caller; DoltSync.syncAfter()'s real value-add over a bare doltPushAfter() call is wrapping it in runDegradable(), which catches an unresolved failure and returns a structured {degraded:true} outcome instead of always throwing.

entries.title: apra-fleet-se's full real-bd test:integration suite takes ~4h; CI only ever runs one file in real mode
entries.summary: The full 'npm run test:integration' (scripts/run-tests.mjs real, no file arg) covers ~129 files against a real bd/dolt engagement and is documented as a once-per-sprint job, not a per-task/per-PR check; it also surfaces unrelated known carry-over regressions.

entries.title: ESM main-module guard must use pathToFileURL, not string interpolation, or it silently no-ops on win32
entries.summary: Comparing import.meta.url to a template-literal file:// string built from process.argv[1] is always false on Windows, so main() never runs -- no crash, just a silent exit 0.

entries.title: A sprint's own reservation is always in GET /api/sprints while it deploys
entries.summary: The supervisor reservation ledger always contains the deploying sprint's own entry, so any 'non-empty sprints array => stop' deploy gate blocks every sprint from deploying its own work; identity must be compared exactly on sprintId.

entries.title: resolveProjectSlug prefers an explicit git remote URL over shelling git against repo_path
entries.summary: resolveProjectSlug(cwd, remoteUrl) slugifies remoteUrl directly when supplied and only falls back to `git remote get-url origin` against cwd, then the repo dirname, then 'default', when no URL is given -- letting remote members (whose repo_path is unreachable from the fleet server host) resolve to the same slug as a local clone.

entries.title: Measure a source-text guard's coverage by line-by-line injection, and count only the before/after delta
entries.summary: Injecting a real violating line at every line of every scanned module, then comparing the old and new checker, is what turns 'the guard scans clean' into evidence. Raw blind-line counts overstate the hole because an injection inside a comment or template text is legitimately not code -- only the delta, plus a classification of the residual, is defensible.

entries.title: dolt-sync.mjs sync.remote/tip memoization is process-lifetime, so multi-scenario tests must reset it between runs
entries.summary: fleet-sprint/dolt-sync.mjs memoizes each member's sync.remote answer and last-synced tip fingerprint in module-level maps for the whole process, so the first mock-sprint scenario in a process dispatches a real probe that later scenarios skip; comparing two runs in one process needs the reset triple between them.

entries.title: SqliteProvider freshness verdicts must be suppressed, not re-hashed, when the repo anchor is unreachable
entries.summary: A repo_path that does not exist on this host (the remote-member case) must never fall back to process.cwd() as the freshness anchor, and must not be re-hashed against it either -- both checkFreshness and freshnessSweep now short-circuit to a no-op verdict via a shared anchorIsMissing() check instead.

entries.title: The sprint runner's dispatch inactivity budget is clamped to 1800s and no longer equals max_total_s
entries.summary: dispatch_timeout_s is applied as max_total_s unchanged, but timeout_s is passed through a min(1800, total) clamp, so the two budgets diverge at every default-args run and code or comments assuming they are equal are wrong.

entries.title: Provider-conditional body markers must be on their own line and cannot be quoted inside a fence
